why: Hand squeezing at 4 litres an hour, a juicer at 20 litres an hour costing $6,630 over two years and a $12 staff cost are believable, and 255 days fits weekday opening.
Each survey row is a subset no larger than the one above it for both small (3,170 to 495) and large (1,428 to 193) offices, so the funnel is consistent.

Wash prices of EUR 2.50 to 4.00, a few hundred customers per laundromat a week and EUR 3 of vending spend are believable, and a 40% vending margin against 12% for the trade is within a factor of a few.
78 cafes taking about $3.4 to $3.8 million a month (roughly $45,000 to $49,000 per cafe) is believable, as are the modest index movements.
Division revenues of EUR 31 to 168 million with margins of 4% to 23%, and print magazines declining, are believable for a publisher.
About $1.75 to $1.96 million of monthly fare revenue across 140 local routes is believable for a regional bus operator, as are the modest index movements.

With 3 small, 5 mid and 4 big-market teams the segment figures reproduce the stated $68.5 million revenue, $4.15 million profit and a 50% average win rate, and the magnitudes are believable for a baseball league.
Hand dividing at 10 kg an hour, a divider at 40 kg an hour costing $13,640 over four years and a $12 wage are believable for a 26-shop bakery chain.
A farm-diesel distributor with $380 million sales, fuel at 94% and operating costs at 7% losing 1% is consistent and believable for a thin-margin fuel distributor.
Module revenues of $1 to $43 million (about $143 million in all) against 6 to 82 developers per module, roughly $460,000 per developer, are believable for a loss-making software firm.
